The Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM) under the Ministry of Finance is the nodal department handling central government disinvestment and asset monetisation.

The New Public Sector Enterprise (NSE) Policy formulated in 2021 classifies strategic sectors (where a bare minimum presence of PSUs is retained) and non-strategic sectors (where PSUs are privatised or closed).
Asset monetisation involves unlocking value from unutilised or under-utilised public assets, such as land, buildings, and operational infrastructure like highways and railways.
Non-debt capital receipts comprise recoveries of loans and proceeds from the sale of government assets, including disinvestment and public enterprise equity stakes.

The Election Commission of India’s (ECI) Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls has brought mass deletions, suspect deletion requests and questions over polling records. India’s first roll holds a lesson: nearly 28 lakh women were left off it, because they were listed only by their relationship to a man.
Inclusion as much as removal: An accurate roll drops dead, shifted and duplicate entries and keeps every eligible voter. It is like a class register that strikes off leavers and adds every new admission.
The first roll’s lesson: Sukumar Sen , India’s first Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) , worked to enrol these women in their own right. By the 1957 elections, about 85% of them had been enrolled.
The takeaway: Correcting a wrongful exclusion matters as much as removing a wrong entry, because a remedy that comes too late results in a lost vote .
Bihar’s missing names: About 65 lakh names were missing from the draft roll published in August 2025 . The ECI cited deaths, migration and duplicate entries.
Court direction: The Supreme Court directed the ECI to publish the excluded voters with reasons, so voters can challenge errors.
West Bengal’s backlog: More than 27 lakh names were deleted during adjudication, prompting around 22 lakh appeals.
Appeal hurdles: Tribunal judges have flagged problems with the appeals portal and with issuing notices, holding hearings and restoring names .
Form 7: Form 7 is the application through which an elector can seek the deletion of a name from the roll.
The Aland case: In Aland, Karnataka, 6,018 online applications sought deletions, and the ECI accepted only 24 after verification.
Safeguards worked: The ECI rejected the other 5,994 as incorrect. An inquiry followed and a First Information Report (FIR) was registered.
Who filed them: A concentrated pattern of requests requires the ECI to establish who submitted them and whether identities or documents were misused.
Maharashtra turnout: Reported turnout in Maharashtra’s last Assembly election rose from 58.22% in the evening to 66.05% in the final count. The ECI called the first figure provisional, but the jump needs explaining.
Polling records rule: The government amended Rule 93 of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 after a Punjab and Haryana High Court order to release election records. This raises concerns over access to CCTV footage and webcasting .

The crisis was triggered by the breakdown of the 2022 Yemen ceasefire in July, leading to al-Houthi occupation of Red Sea plains.
The core issue is the extreme vulnerability of Saudi oil exports and critical maritime routes to combined attacks from state and militia actors.

According to the minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meeting held from October 5 to 7, released by the RBI on Wednesday, Malhotra said the duration and extent of the current rate-hiking cycle would depend on how inflationary pressures evolve. "Nevertheless, I feel it is appropriate to change the stance to calibrated tightening, essentially signalling that rate cuts are off the table in the near term and policy action ahead can only be a rate hike or a pause, depending on the evolving circumstances and the outlook," Malhotra stated. The remarks come after the MPC unanimously raised the policy repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50 per cent earlier this month and shifted its monetary policy stance to calibrated tightening amid rising inflationary pressures. The RBI Governor highlighted growing signs that inflation was spreading across a wider range of goods and services, raising concerns about the persistence of price pressures. "In terms of the diffusion index, there are increasing signs of generalisation of inflation as 37 per cent of the commodities in the CPI basket had inflation above 4 per cent in August – it was merely 20 per cent in March," he said.

New Delhi: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Wednesday shared an article by Union Ministers Pralhad Joshi and Shivraj Singh Chouhan that highlighted the potential of agrivoltaics to strengthen farmers' incomes by combining solar power generation with agricultural activity. In a post on social media platform X, the Prime Minister said the technology could provide farmers with an additional source of revenue, lower energy costs and support crop productivity, describing it as an important avenue for advancing rural prosperity. Notably, India will host the seventh AgriVoltaics World Conference here from October 21 to October 23 under the theme ‘Powering the Global South’.

According to the ministers, the model can generate additional income from electricity sales, reduce dependence on diesel and purchased power, and create favourable microclimatic conditions that help protect crops from heat stress, drought, excessive solar radiation and hail. They also stated that wider adoption of agrivoltaics could stimulate rural employment through installation, maintenance and agricultural services linked to solar infrastructure. They stressed that successful deployment would require suitable crop selection, adequate irrigation and nutrient management, as well as designs that preserve sufficient sunlight for cultivation.

Two previously unknown subterranean fish species have been discovered in wells in Assam's Goalpara district, state environment and forests minister Jayanta Malla Baruah said on Wednesday. Gitchak nakana measures around two centimetres and has a reddish appearance because its transparent body reveals its blood and internal organs.
Rakthamichthys anchi, meanwhile, is a slender subterranean fish belonging to the swamp eel family. Both species are adapted to life in underground groundwater environments, making their discovery particularly significant for scientific research. The specimens were collected by researcher Wimarithy K. Marak, who shared a photograph with her supervisor.
The second discovery followed when one of her relatives found another subterranean fish while cleaning a well, the minister said. MUMBAI, Oct 21 (Reuters) - India should allow the dollar-rupee exchange rate to move as the first line of defence amid the ongoing oil shock, an IMF official said on Wednesday.
"Our advice to countries is to use the exchange rate as the first line of defence amid ongoing shocks," Krishna Srinivasan, director of the Asia and Pacific Department at the IMF, said at a media briefing in Mumbai. "We would advise India to let the exchange rate move."
The Reserve Bank of India has intervened heavily to support the rupee via dollar sales from its reserves, a special window to offer dollars to oil companies and reserve requirements for large hedge requirements.
The rupee, which fell to near record lows earlier this month has rebounded about 2% following the central bank's steps.
Foreign-exchange interventions have not been particularly beneficial beyond the near term due to the oil shock, Srinivasan said, adding that exchange rates have to be shock absorbers.
In June, India also cut taxes on foreign investments in government debt and raised $134 billion via a dollar deposit scheme targeted at the Indian diaspora.
The forex measures taken by the RBI in June like cutting taxes on foreign debt investments were largely positive as they encouraged capital inflows, said Ranil Salgado, senior representative for India, Bhutan and Maldives at the IMF.
